claims.text: Self-consistency checking alone is insufficient to identify question-level and model-level hallucinations in language models.
SAC3-Q achieves an AUROC of 99.4% on the Prime number classification QA dataset.
SAC3-Q achieves an AUROC of 97.0% on the Senator search classification QA dataset.
SAC3-QM with Guanaco-33b achieves an AUROC score of 88.0% on the HotpotQA-halu generation QA dataset.
SAC3-Q achieves an AUROC score of 77.2% on the NQ-open-halu open-domain generation QA task.
The performance gains of SAC3 plateau after using more than 5 perturbed question samples.

evidence.description: When prompted with 'Is pi smaller than 3.2?', ChatGPT consistently generates incorrect answers, demonstrating that consistent responses can still be non-factual and evade self-consistency checks.
In balanced classification QA tasks, SAC3-Q achieves an AUROC of 99.4% on Prime number compared to 65.9% for the SC2 self-consistency baseline.
In balanced classification QA tasks, SAC3-Q achieves an AUROC of 97.0% on Senator search compared to 56.1% for the SC2 self-consistency baseline.
In open-domain generation QA tasks, SAC3-QM using Guanaco-33b achieves 88.0% AUROC on HotpotQA-halu, an improvement over SC2's 74.2% AUROC.
In open-domain generation QA tasks, SAC3-Q achieves 77.2% AUROC on NQ-open-halu, improving upon SC2's 70.5% AUROC.
Varying the number of perturbed questions k from 2 to 10 shows that performance increases up to k=5 and then diminishes in marginal returns.

methodologies.name: Semantic-aware Cross-check Consistency (SAC3)
methodologies.description: A sampling-based hallucination detection framework for black-box language models that expands on self-consistency by incorporating semantically equivalent question perturbations and cross-model verifier response checking.
conditions: Temperature 0.0 for question perturbation and consistency check
k=10 semantically equivalent question perturbations by default

limitations.text: Uncertainty metrics based on token-level log probabilities require full white-box internal model access, which is unavailable in black-box commercial LMs offering only API access.
Evaluation is restricted to question-answering settings and does not assess generalizability to complex conversational or dialogue-based tasks.
Increasing sample sizes to improve detection accuracy introduces additional computational cost and inference latency.
Model-level cross-checking fails to accurately detect hallucinations when verifier LMs refuse to answer questions due to lack of information.

future_work.text: Assess the generalizability of the SAC3 framework and semantic equivalence checks on complex tasks such as conversational or dialogue-based prompting.
Investigate optimization and parallelization strategies to speed up implementation and balance the efficiency-utility trade-off.
